subChunks.title: Custom Design Token Systems
subChunks.hookHtml: A design token system is the contract between design and engineering. When implemented well in Tailwind v4's @theme, every design decision is a CSS variable — and changing the brand colour, spacing scale, or typography requires touching one file, not one thousand. This lesson builds a complete token system from first principles.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Grand Archmage Solomon: "A design token is not a variable. It is an intent. --color-brand-600 is not 'the hex value I chose today.' It is 'the primary interactive colour of this product.' That distinction matters when the product changes, the designer changes, or the client changes."

The token hierarchy

/* 3 levels of tokens: primitive → semantic → component */

/* Level 1: Primitive — raw values, named by scale */
@theme {
  --color-indigo-50:  oklch(0.97 0.02 270);
  --color-indigo-100: oklch(0.93 0.04 270);
  --color-indigo-500: oklch(0.55 0.20 270);
  --color-indigo-900: oklch(0.25 0.10 270);
}

/* Level 2: Semantic — intent, not value */
@theme {
  --color-primary:            var(--color-indigo-500);
  --color-primary-light:      var(--color-indigo-100);
  --color-primary-foreground: oklch(0.99 0 0);
  --color-surface:            oklch(0.99 0 0);
  --color-surface-raised:     oklch(0.96 0 0);
  --color-foreground:         oklch(0.15 0 0);
  --color-muted:              oklch(0.60 0 0);
  --color-border:             oklch(0.90 0 0);
  --color-error:              oklch(0.55 0.20 25);
  --color-success:            oklch(0.55 0.18 155);
  --color-warning:            oklch(0.75 0.15 80);
}

/* Level 3: Component — specific usage */
@theme {
  --color-btn-primary-bg:     var(--color-primary);
  --color-btn-primary-text:   var(--color-primary-foreground);
  --color-input-border:       var(--color-border);
  --color-input-focus:        var(--color-primary);
}

Fluid typography with clamp()

/* Fluid font sizes that scale smoothly between breakpoints */
@theme {
  --font-size-fluid-sm: clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.375vw, 1rem);
  --font-size-fluid-md: clamp(1rem, 0.9rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem);
  --font-size-fluid-lg: clamp(1.25rem, 1rem + 1.25vw, 2rem);
  --font-size-fluid-xl: clamp(2rem, 1.5rem + 2.5vw, 3.5rem);
}

/* Usage: */
<h1 class="text-[var(--font-size-fluid-xl)] font-bold">Hero Title</h1>

oklch() — the correct colour space for design tokens

/* oklch(lightness chroma hue) */
/* lightness: 0 = black, 1 = white */
/* chroma: 0 = gray, higher = more saturated */
/* hue: 0–360 (red=25, yellow=80, green=155, blue=250, purple=300) */

/* Creating a coherent colour ramp: */
@theme {
  --color-brand-50:  oklch(0.97 0.02 270);  /* very light */
  --color-brand-100: oklch(0.93 0.05 270);
  --color-brand-200: oklch(0.86 0.09 270);
  --color-brand-300: oklch(0.78 0.13 270);
  --color-brand-400: oklch(0.68 0.17 270);
  --color-brand-500: oklch(0.58 0.20 270);  /* main brand */
  --color-brand-600: oklch(0.50 0.20 270);
  --color-brand-700: oklch(0.42 0.18 270);
  --color-brand-800: oklch(0.34 0.15 270);
  --color-brand-900: oklch(0.24 0.10 270);  /* very dark */
}

/* Advantage over hex: perceptual uniformity — each step looks
   equally different from the next. hex ramps are often visually
   uneven at the light and dark extremes. */

Spacing scale customisation

@theme {
  /* Extend the default scale with project-specific values */
  --spacing-18:  4.5rem;   /* 72px — common section padding */
  --spacing-88:  22rem;    /* 352px — sidebar width */
  --spacing-112: 28rem;    /* 448px — dialog max-width */
  --spacing-128: 32rem;    /* 512px — content column */
}

Border radius tokens

@theme {
  --radius-sm:  4px;
  --radius-md:  8px;
  --radius-lg:  12px;
  --radius-xl:  16px;
  --radius-2xl: 24px;
  --radius-pill: 9999px;
}

/* Usage: rounded-[var(--radius-xl)] or define via @layer */

Solomon: "A complete token system answers: what is every possible value for colour, spacing, typography, radius, and shadow in this product? If you cannot answer from the CSS file, the design system is incomplete."

storyBeats.speaker: Grand Archmage Solomon
storyBeats.text: Three levels: primitive (raw values), semantic (intent), component (usage). A colour rebrand changes primitives. A theme change changes semantics. Component code never changes. That is a well-designed token system.

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a token-driven design system card. These classes simulate a fully configured @theme system:

  • .token-card: bg-white, border, border-gray-200, rounded-2xl, p-6, shadow-sm
  • .token-swatch-row: flex, gap-2, flex-wrap, mb-4
  • .token-swatch: w-10, h-10, rounded-lg
  • .token-label: text-xs, font-mono, text-gray-500, mt-1
  • .token-divider: border-t, border-gray-100, my-4
  • .token-heading: text-sm, font-semibold, text-gray-700, mb-3

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Design a complete @theme token system for a SaaS product from scratch. Define: a 9-step colour scale for your brand using oklch(), 5 semantic tokens (primary, surface, foreground, muted, border), 3 fluid typography sizes using clamp(), and 4 custom spacing values. Then build a card using only your semantic tokens — no raw utility colours. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the three-level token hierarchy (primitive, semantic, component) with a concrete colour example. Why does using oklch() give you a better colour ramp than hex? Walk through what happens to components when a brand colour is rebranded in a well-designed token system.

questions.prompt: In oklch(lightness chroma hue), what does the chroma value control?
options: Saturation — 0 produces gray, higher values produce more vivid colour
Transparency — 0 is transparent, 1 is fully opaque
Hue rotation — offsets the hue by the chroma value in degrees
questions.answer: Saturation — 0 produces gray, higher values produce more vivid colour
questions.explanation: In oklch: lightness (0=black, 1=white), chroma (0=gray/achromatic, increasing = more saturated colour), hue (0–360 degrees: ~25=red, ~80=yellow, ~155=green, ~250=blue, ~300=purple). oklch is perceptually uniform — equal increments in lightness look equally different to the human eye.

questions.prompt: What is the advantage of the three-level token hierarchy (primitive → semantic → component) over using raw colour utilities directly in components?
options: A brand colour change requires updating only the primitive token — semantic and component tokens reference it via var(), so all components update automatically
It adds type safety — TypeScript can validate the token names
It reduces CSS file size — fewer unique values are emitted
It makes dark mode automatic — semantic tokens resolve correctly in both themes
questions.answer: A brand colour change requires updating only the primitive token — semantic and component tokens reference it via var(), so all components update automatically
questions.explanation: The primitive --color-brand-500 is referenced by semantic --color-primary: var(--color-brand-500), which is used in every component. Changing --color-brand-500: oklch(0.53 0.17 155) (from indigo to teal) propagates through all three levels without touching a single component file. Dark mode is a separate concern — the semantic layer also handles that by reassigning variable values.

questions.prompt: A design spec has h1 at 32px on mobile and 56px on desktop (1280px). Which @theme declaration creates a fluid font size that scales smoothly between these breakpoints?
options: Fluid typography requires JavaScript — CSS cannot interpolate between breakpoints
questions.explanation: clamp(min, preferred, max) creates a fluid value. With clamp(2rem, 1.5rem + 2.5vw, 3.5rem): at 320px viewport the preferred (1.5rem + 2.5vw ≈ 2rem) hits the minimum; at 1280px it reaches ~3.5rem. The font scales smoothly between breakpoints without JavaScript or media queries.
